demo_0.title: Efficient Algorithms for Counterfactual Regret Minimization
demo_0.abstract: We propose a novel algorithm for Counterfactual regret minimization that achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining computational efficiency. Our method combines theoretical insights with practical optimizations, demonstrating significant improvements over existing approaches on standard benchmarks.

demo_1.title: Neural Counterfactual Regret Minimization: End-to-End Learning
demo_1.abstract: This paper proposes an end-to-end neural framework for Counterfactual regret minimization. By integrating representation learning with decision-making, our approach achieves superior performance compared to traditional pipeline methods. We provide theoretical analysis of the learned representations.

demo_2.title: Towards Counterfactual Regret Minimization: Challenges and Opportunities
demo_2.abstract: An analysis of the current challenges and emerging opportunities in Counterfactual regret minimization. We examine the gap between theoretical guarantees and practical performance, discuss the role of large-scale pretraining, and outline the path toward real-world deployment of these methods.

demo_3.title: Optimization Methods for Counterfactual Regret Minimization
demo_3.abstract: We develop optimization-based approaches for Counterfactual regret minimization that provide stronger theoretical guarantees. Our method achieves faster convergence rates through novel variance reduction techniques. Experiments on challenging benchmarks confirm the advantages.

demo_4.title: A Unified Algorithmic Framework for Counterfactual Regret Minimization
demo_4.abstract: We propose a unified framework that encompasses many existing algorithms for Counterfactual regret minimization as special cases. This abstraction enables principled comparisons and reveals new algorithmic variants with improved performance characteristics.
